text:
The Jets spent most of Sunday building a 3-0 lead the right way and about 26 seconds watching it disappear. Then Mark Scheifele put a power-play slap shot in with 1.6 seconds left, and Winnipeg had its third straight win.

For two and a half periods this was Winnipeg's game, and the power play was the reason. Cole Perfetti scored on it early in the second, Morgan Barron added a slap shot at even strength, and Brayden Yager, the 14th pick of the 2023 draft, scored his first NHL goal on another power play at 8:10 of the third. The Jets went 3 for 5 with the man advantage, 2.31 expected goals' worth, while Tampa Bay went 0 for 4. Over the whole night Winnipeg deserved to win 77% of the time.

Tampa Bay never quits on these, and Brandon Hagel's goal at 10:22 started it. Pontus Holmberg, a sixth-round pick by Toronto in 2018 and the most unlikely hero on the ice, then scored at 14:01 and again at 14:27, the second a backhand on a 57% chance. That swing took the Lightning from a 12% win chance to 48%. Andrei Vasilevskiy kept it there with a stop on Perfetti late, the biggest save of the night, before Scheifele's winner.

The cost for Tampa Bay may outlast the result. Brayden Point left in the first period after 5:35 of ice time, and Jon Cooper said he might miss some time; Point came in on a seven-game, 10-point streak. All of it plays out under the Nikita Kucherov trade request, which has Vasilevskiy telling TSN he hopes "that something will change." Winnipeg, for its part, has bigger news coming: Connor Hellebuyck returns with the Devils on Tuesday, though New Jersey says he won't start.
headline: Holmberg ties it, Scheifele wins it with 1.6 left
